text:
maria: heads-up — deploybot blocked the staging image publish from CI run 1234. Error says ephemeral tag already in use, aborted publish. We need a quick call: retag & republish now, or pin canary to previous digest and schedule republish in next change window?
deploybot: publish attempt failed for repo=redwood/staging, tag=staging-2026-03-21-1234, error=EphemeralTagCollision: tag currently referenced by another pending upload. logs: `PUT /v2/redwood/staging/manifests/staging-2026-03-21-1234 -> 409`
dan: can we just retag to a non-ephemeral name and push? eg `staging-1234-retag-489876` then update canary route. That avoids blocking. I'll do the push if infra signs off.
sara: retagging is fine but note: provenance attestation job ties to original build metadata. If we retag and skip reattestation, canary may fail our release checks. Safer path: pin canary to the previous digest (sha256:111111aaa...) for the immediate window, then run a republish+attest in the maintenance window.
nate: oncall here — if we pin canary to previous digest, I can keep traffic routing to the pinned digest at 5% and monitor for 60m. If performance looks good we can escalate traffic. What are the rollback steps if the republish produces different behavior?
maria: good call. Let's do temp pin for canary, then a controlled republish with attestation in the 01:00-03:00 UTC change window. Nate: please keep 5% for 30-60m. Dan: if you republish outside the window we may need an explicit approval from product.
dan: ok I'll prepare the retag & republish playbook now. Plan: 1) pull manifest from CI artifact store, 2) `aws ecr put-image --repository redwood/staging --image-tag staging-1234-retag-489876 --image-manifest file://manifest.json`, 3) run `cosign sign --keyring /keys/cosign-key staging-1234-retag-489876`, 4) push provenance metadata to attest-bucket.
sara: small tweak — step 2 should include `--image-manifest` that exactly matches the original manifest (no layer rewrite), otherwise digest changes and previous pins break. Also we need to re-run `attest` job: `./scripts/attest-manifest.sh --repo redwood/staging --tag staging-1234-retag-489876`.
olivia: I'll draft a short release note blurb: "Staging: temporary pin applied due to ephemeral tag collision during CI publish. Republish & attestation scheduled 01:00-03:00 UTC. No consumer impact expected." Dan, pull the final digest after republish so I can include it.
dan: doing the retag now in staging sandbox to validate. command used: `aws ecr put-image --repository redwood/staging --image-tag staging-1234-retag-489876 --image-manifest "$(cat /tmp/ci/manifest-1234.json)"`
dan: result: pushed as sha256:abcdef1234567890. deploybot webhook shows `PUBLISH_OK` for tag=staging-1234-retag-489876 but attest job queued: `attest-job-id=attest-489876-1`.
sara: attest job started: logs show `cosign: signing manifest sha256:abcdef1234567890` then `upload provenance -> s3://attestations/staging/abcdef1234.json`.
maria: excellent. Nate — start canary routing to pinned digest sha256:111111aaa... at 5% now, and then switch to staging-1234-retag-489876 at 5% after attestation is green. Please post metrics if error rate > 0.5% or latency 95p spikes. :eyes:
nate: pin applied to sha256:111111aaa... at 22:14 UTC, monitoring. If everything looks stable after 30m I'll flip 5% to the new digest and run a 30m observation.
dan: publish & attest done. New digest sha256:abcdef1234567890 is live for canary after attestation. deploybot posted success: `deploybot: attestation verified, canary rollout allowed.` :shipit:
maria: Olivia, update release notes with both digests and mention the maintenance window. Also log the decision in the release channel. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
